data.name: Sabhajeet
data.gender_notes: Sabhajeet is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Sabhajeet is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Sabha' meaning assembly or gathering and 'Jeet' meaning victory. The name Sabhajeet signifies the victory of a sage or a wise man. The name Sabhajeet carries the meaning “Sage's Victory” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Bengali, Marathi. Parents who choose Sabhajeet usually hope their child will grow to embody sage's victory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Sabhajeet is a spiritual name that signifies the victory of wisdom and knowledge over ignorance and darkness. It is a name that is often given to children who are believed to have a strong potential for spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Sabhajeet belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sage's Victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sabhajeet total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sabhajeet, signifying the victory of a wise man or sage, can be deeply rooted in the ancient wisdom-centric culture of the Indian subcontinent. Sabhajeet can be a powerful reminder of the ancient values of knowledge, wisdom, and triumph that have shaped Indian civilization for millennia. The name evokes the image of famous sages and seers who have left an indelible impact on Indian culture, including the likes of Maharishi Valmiki, Mahatma Vyasa, and Maharshi Ved Vyasa. In recent times, this name evokes the image of modern-day scholars, thinkers, and educators who are leading the way in various fields of study and thought.

historical_references.reference: Sabhajeet was a renowned scholar and philosopher during the Gupta Empire (circa 4th to 6th century CE). He is known for his contributions to the Jain philosophy and wrote several commentaries on the major Jain texts.

Another reference attributes Sabhajeet to the Vakpati Gommateshwara dynasty (10th to 12th century CE) in the Deccan region of present-day India. He was a Jain monk and a prominent figure in the development of the Digambara sect.
